Amin al-Husseini.fact: 1897 – 4 July 1974) was a Palestinian Arab nationalist and Muslim leader in Mandatory Palestine.

Amin al-Husseini.subject: Indian Languages
Amin al-Husseini.question: Husseini was born in _____, Ottoman Empire in 1897, he received education in Islamic, Ottoman, and Catholic schools
Amin al-Husseini.fact: He was the scion of the al-Husayni family of Jerusalemite Arab nobles, who trace their origins to the Islamic prophet Muhammad. Husseini was born in Jerusalem, Ottoman Empire in 1897, he received education in Islamic, Ottoman, and Catholic schools.

Amin al-Husseini.subject: Indian Languages
Amin al-Husseini.question: In 1921, Herbert Samuel, the _____ appointed him Grand Mufti of Jerusalem, a position he used to promote Islam while rallying a non-confessional Arab nationalism against Zionism
Amin al-Husseini.fact: In 1921, Herbert Samuel, the British High Commissioner appointed him Grand Mufti of Jerusalem, a position he used to promote Islam while rallying a non-confessional Arab nationalism against Zionism.

Amin al-Husseini.subject: Indian Languages
Amin al-Husseini.question: In the lead-up to the 1948 _____ war, Husseini opposed both the 1947 UN Partition Plan and Jordan's plan to annex the West Bank
Amin al-Husseini.fact: In 1937, evading an arrest warrant for aligning himself against British rule as leader of the 1936–1939 Arab revolt in Palestine, he fled and took refuge in Lebanon and afterwards Iraq. He then set up himself in Fascist Italy and Nazi Germany, which he collaborated with during World War II against Britain, requesting during a meeting with Adolf Hitler backing for Arab independence and opposition to the establishment of a Jewish national home in Palestine.

Amin al-Husseini.subject: Indian Languages
Amin al-Husseini.question: In September 1948 he participated in the establishment of an All-_____ in Egyptian-ruled Gaza, but this government won limited recognition and was eventually dissolved by Egypt in 1959
Amin al-Husseini.fact: In September 1948 he participated in the establishment of an All-Palestine Government in Egyptian-ruled Gaza, but this government won limited recognition and was eventually dissolved by Egypt in 1959.

Amin al-Husseini.subject: Indian Languages
Amin al-Husseini.question: After the war and the 1948 _____ expulsion and flight, his claims to leadership were discredited and he was eventually sidelined by the establishment of the Palestine Liberation Organization in 1964
Amin al-Husseini.fact: After the war and the 1948 Palestinian expulsion and flight, his claims to leadership were discredited and he was eventually sidelined by the establishment of the Palestine Liberation Organization in 1964.

Amin al-Husseini.subject: Indian Languages
Amin al-Husseini.question: Thirteen members of the clan had been Mayors of _____ between 1864 and 1920
Amin al-Husseini.fact: The al-Husseini clan consisted of wealthy landowners in southern Palestine, centered around the district of Jerusalem. Thirteen members of the clan had been Mayors of Jerusalem between 1864 and 1920.

Amin al-Husseini.subject: Indian Languages
Amin al-Husseini.question: Though groomed to hold religious office from youth, his education was typical of the _____ effendi at the time, and he only donned a religious turban in 1921 after being appointed mufti
Amin al-Husseini.fact: Though groomed to hold religious office from youth, his education was typical of the Ottoman effendi at the time, and he only donned a religious turban in 1921 after being appointed mufti. Prior to World War I, he studied at the School of Administration in Constantinople, the most secular of Ottoman institutions.

Amin al-Husseini.subject: Indian Languages
Amin al-Husseini.question: In 1913, approximately at the age of 16, al-_____ accompanied his mother Zainab to Mecca and received the honorary title of Hajji
Amin al-Husseini.fact: However, Al-Husseini did not adopt his teacher's Islamic fundamentalism. In 1913, approximately at the age of 16, al-Husseini accompanied his mother Zainab to Mecca and received the honorary title of Hajji.

Amin al-Husseini.subject: Indian Languages

Amin al-Husseini.fact: In November 1916 he obtained a three-month disability leave from the army and returned to Jerusalem. Amin al-Husseini.fact: He accepted the pardon only in the wake of the death of his half-brother, the mufti Kamil al-Husayni, in March 1921. A year earlier the British had replaced Musa al-Husayni as Mayor of Jerusalem with Raghib al-Nashashibi.

Amin al-Husseini.fact: Worldwide Jewish protests remonstrated with Britain for the violence exercised at the Wall.
